title: Classes (OOP)
bro_quote: Objects organize code into logic bundles—classes are how Python structures large programs.

subtopics.name: What is a Class?
subtopics.explanation:
• 🏠 A class is a blueprint for creating objects. Like an architectural plan before building houses.
  • 🎯 An object is an instance created from that class. Each house built from the plan is different.
  • 📦 Classes group related data (attributes) and actions (methods) together.
  • 🔤 Class names usually start with capital letters by convention. Example: Dog, Person.

snippets.code:
class Dog:
    pass

my_dog = Dog()
print(my_dog)

subtopics.name: Attributes and __init__
subtopics.explanation:
• ⚙️ __init__ is the constructor — it runs when you create an object.
  • 🏷️ Set up initial data (attributes) inside __init__.
  • 🔗 self refers to the specific object being created.
  • 💾 Attributes are stored as self.attribute_name

snippets.code:
dog1 = Dog("Buddy", 3)
dog2 = Dog("Max", 5)
print(dog1.name)  # Buddy
print(dog2.name)  # Max

subtopics.name: Methods (Actions)
subtopics.explanation:
• ⚙️ Methods are functions inside a class that perform actions.
  • 🔗 First parameter is always self — refers to the object calling the method.
  • 🎯 Call methods using dot notation: object.method()
  • 📊 Methods can access and modify the object's attributes.

subtopics.name: Understanding self
subtopics.explanation:
• 🔗 self is a reference to the current object. It's how methods know which object is calling them.
  • 🎯 You don't pass self manually — Python does it automatically.
  • 📦 Use self.attribute to access the object's data.
  • 💡 When you call object.method(), Python converts it to Class.method(object) behind the scenes.

subtopics.name: Instance Attributes vs Class Attributes
subtopics.explanation:
• 👤 Instance attributes belong to individual objects. Set in __init__ with self.
  • 🏫 Class attributes belong to the whole class. Defined outside methods, shared by all instances.
  • 📊 Each object has its own copy of instance attributes. Changing one doesn't affect others.

snippets.code:
class Animal:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name      # Instance attribute

dog = Animal("Buddy")
cat = Animal("Whiskers")
dog.name = "Max"  # Only dog changes
print(dog.name)   # Max
print(cat.name)   # Whiskers (unchanged)

subtopics.name: Building a Complete Class
subtopics.explanation:
• 🏗️ Combine __init__, attributes, and methods to create useful classes.
  • 🎯 Design classes to represent real-world objects or concepts.
  • 📝 Good classes have clear purposes and well-organized code.

questions: 1. Define an empty class named Robot. (Defining class)
2. Add an __init__ method to initialize a robot's name. (Init method)
3. Create a specific instance (object) from your class and store it in a variable. (Creating instance)
4. Print out the name attribute of your created instance. (Instance attribute)
5. Write a method inside the class that makes the robot say 'Beep boop!'. (Instance method)
6. Create two entirely separate robot instances with different names. (Multiple instances)
7. Change the name attribute of one of your robots after it has been created. (Modifying attributes)
8. Call the speaking method you wrote on one of your robot instances. (Calling methods)
9. Understand the 'self' parameter by writing a method that prints the robot's own name. (Self parameter)
10. Create a method that takes an external parameter and adds it to the robot's power level. (Method parameters)
